purpose: THE RUBY APPLICABLE SET as a machine-readable table: one row per canonical relationship type the Ruby language can express (decided from the PINNED GRAMMAR's own enumeration, never from the ten-value matrix), with the emission site in src/ast/real-ruby-analyzer.ts and at least one fixture that can go RED for it — plus the ruled non-applicable canonical values.

admissibilityRule: A canonical value is APPLICABLE to Ruby iff (i) every construct production it needs is present in the pinned grammar's enumeration, (ii) src/ast/real-ruby-analyzer.ts has an emission site for it, (iii) at least one committed fixture carries a positive `expectRelationships` row naming it, and (iv) that fixture goes RED when the emission is removed (measured through the real fixture runner). A value ruled NOT APPLICABLE must have ZERO emissions over the fixture corpus (positive evidence of absence).

calls.rule: a `call` whose callee is not a builtin; bare identifiers in expression position that are not locals are calls (`bareCall: true`); source = enclosing method, else owner, else the file-scope sentinel; receiver calls keep the leaf target.

uses.rule: instance-variable READS (`memberRead`) and ActiveRecord association macros (`activerecordMacro`); writes including compound-assignment LHS stay silent.

contains.rule: one edge per OWNED symbol from `ownerName`; a factory-declared type owns its DSL block's members, a bare unnamed `Class.new do … end` owns nothing (NAMABLE-OWNER rule); the line is the naming token (#825).

imports.rule: `require`/`require_relative`/`load`/`autoload` — one `imports` edge per required path (file-level, `requireMethod`, `resolution: file-relative|load-path`) written one-for-one with the `imports[]` payload channel and with the `references` row.

references.rule: constant/scope-resolution mentions in read/type positions plus the require/load path strings (the references half of the load-fact pair).

exports.rule: ADAPTED SEMANTICS, declared: Ruby has no export keyword, but a FILE UNIT has a reachable surface — top-level constants/defs, source = the file unit (path-derived, `resolvedTarget: file-unit`), with measured refusals (singleton-class members, `private_constant`, reopens/duplicates are one unit, unnameable symbols).

extends.rule: `class B < A` when the base is a statically nameable constant path (line = the base type node, #825), plus the factory spelling `K = Class.new(Base)`; `extend M` is NOT here any more (RUBY-D1: it is a mixin, mixes_in).

mixes_in.rule: CANONICAL mixin composition (RUBY-D1): `include M`/`prepend M` compose M into the class's ancestor chain, `extend M` into its singleton class; source = composing class/module, target = the mixin, `metadata.mixinType` records the keyword; dynamic (lowercase/computed) arguments emit nothing.
mixes_in.relabel: RUBY-D1: the family's previous adaptation (include/prepend -> implements, extend -> extends) is replaced at the UNCHANGED construct sites; cap-50 delta: implements 17 -> 0, extends -4, mixes_in 0 -> 21 = 17 + 4 EXACTLY, TABLE 1 totals byte-identical.

overrides.rule: a subclass method redefining a base method: 0.95 structural when the base method is verifiable from local declarations or the project companion index, 0.5 with `reasonCode: first-parent-guess` (the declared-cause channel — 84 causeOK on the cap-50 stride).

instantiates.rule: `X.new` on a constant receiver; a receiverless `new` names the enclosing class (`resolvedTarget: enclosing-class`); expression/variable receivers emit nothing (RB-A).

implements.reason: Ruby has no interface/conformance construct — no keyword, no production, no enforcement; duck typing is not a declared conformance. The edges this lane used to publish under implements are include/prepend module composition, which RUBY-D1 now spells mixes_in.
implements.measuredAbsence: 0 implements edges over the whole fixture corpus (11 files) after the relabel; cap-50 implements 17 -> 0 with the TABLE total byte-identical (relabel closure).
implements.vocabularyRuling: canonical value, NOT APPLICABLE to Ruby after RUBY-D1. The previous adaptation is RECORDED, not erased.

decorates.reason: no decorator/annotation production exists in the pinned Ruby grammar; attr_*/ActiveRecord macros are DSL CALLS (carried as contains members / uses), not applied decorators.
decorates.vocabularyRuling: extended value, NOT APPLICABLE to Ruby.

renders.reason: no JSX/element-construction production; ERB/HTML templates are other languages routed to their own analyzers.
renders.vocabularyRuling: extended value (TSX/JSX), NOT APPLICABLE to Ruby.

part_of.reason: Ruby's file-inclusion construct is require/load, published as imports+references; there is no shared-scope part-file directive.
part_of.vocabularyRuling: extended value (Dart part/part of), NOT APPLICABLE to Ruby.

rulings.RUBY-D1: include/prepend/extend are MODULE MIXIN COMPOSITION -> canonical mixes_in (source = composing class/module, target = mixin, metadata.mixinType = keyword). The family's previous adaptation (include/prepend -> implements, extend -> extends) was WRONG on both axes: implements is conformance (Ruby has none) and extend is not superclass inheritance (it composes into the singleton class). Relabel at unchanged sites, delta closure-measured: implements 17 -> 0, extends 48 -> 44, mixes_in 0 -> 21 (17 + 4), TABLE 1 totals byte-identical. Dart's §9.8 relabel is the precedent.
